results.label: this tree ships the M110 news-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
exactly ONE shipped file builds the blackout sentence, so the rule has a single voice and no reader invents its own wording
no shipped file reads a single `window_min` off a news payload any more: the removed knob has no dangling reader
the three readers that DO exist each take the engine’s blackout rather than rebuilding it: the playlist guard, the headline and the setup payload
no shipped client reads the new `windows` echo either, so the API’s provenance block cannot be mistaken for a control by an old page
the served payload has no top-level `window_min` any more — the one-number field is gone, not deprecated
each blocked release carries the window of ITS OWN side (the 45-minute settle, not the 5-minute block)
the payload echoes the pair as provenance, with the source of each side, so a consumer can audit what was applied
a genuinely empty week yields a clear payload that is distinguishable from a blocked one but not from an outage (that gap is M111, and this probe names it as such)
the desk playlist renders the blackout as exactly one guard, quoted verbatim from the engine
and it is a BLOCK-level guard, not a warning the trader can scroll past
with a clear calendar the playlist adds no news guard at all: the “no releases in the window” statement lives in the setup row where the window can be named
an M111 outage reaches this consumer as silence: no guard, no unavailable flag and no error on the payload — the failure is visible only at the market layer, which is exactly the gap M111 measures
a release whose block has not started yet (20 minutes out, 5-minute block) produces no guard, and the payload says why
the setup payload emits `news_blackout` inside its filters block, which is where a downstream alert reads the rule from
with a blackout the setup payload carries it, and with none it is null rather than an empty string or a false
the news check keeps its recorded weight and label: this milestone split a window, it did not retune the grade
the advisory channel answers its calendar surface, and says it cannot fetch rather than inventing a window
that answer names the surface it cannot read and cites where the fact comes from, so the silence is attributable rather than a quiet market
and the channel’s own source declares it cannot fetch, so a later calendar change cannot quietly turn it into a news oracle
the same calendar blocks this desk (5-minute block, 45 settle) and its different pair is reported per account, not once globally
the blackout string a consumer quotes names THIS desk’s two numbers, so one trader’s guard can never describe another’s window

scope: M110 consumers: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock and a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser; two asymmetric news clocks, no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
